In turn for the appointment, they are said to have
each signed a pledge form supporting Wang Ching Wei's
cause. Chen's salary is $600 per mensem while
the other committee members receive $300 each monthly.
In addition a monthly sum of $5,000 has been granted
to the Committee for use in buying over the allegiance
of local middle and primary schools at the rate of
between $100 and $200 per month for middle schools
and between $50 and $80 for primary schools. It
is reported that up to the present time some 50
schools have joined Chen and thus benefited by this
money; the names of the schools however cannot be
ascertained at present.

Because of fear of reprisals from the Chung-
king Government the Committee have so far refused to
conduct the pro-Wang movement in the open, despite
repeated persuasion from their employers. The
latter insisted upon the former making public their
support of Wang's cause for the following reasons :-
to prevent the committee members from reverting in
future, to convince the public of the extent of Wang's
influence in Shanghai and to induce others to join.

Becoming impatient with the secretive
attitude of these followers, Wang's clique decided
to employ indirect methods to force their hands.
page_data.zh:
(3)

（    ）中学，
吴志仙，上海女子大学校长，大沽路451号。

据称，作为任职的交换条件，他们每人都签署了一份支持汪精卫事业的保证书。陈继曾的月薪为600元，其他委员每人每月领取300元。此外，委员会每月还获得5000元的拨款，用于收买当地中小学的效忠，中学每月100至200元，小学每月50至80元。据报道，截至目前，约有50所学校加入了陈继曾的阵营并从中受益；然而，目前尚无法查明这些学校的名称。

由于害怕重庆政府的报复，尽管雇主反复劝说，该委员会至今拒绝公开开展亲汪运动。后者坚持要求前者公开支持汪氏事业，理由如下：防止委员会成员日后反悔，让公众相信汪氏在上海的影响力范围，并诱使其他人加入。

汪精卫派系对这些追随者的秘密态度感到不耐烦，决定采取间接手段迫使他们就范。

page_data.en:
(4)

Suddenly on August 13, 1939 a letter alleged to
have been signed by Chen Chi Zung in support of Wang's
peace movement appeared in the Sin Shun Pao while
a similar letter alleged to have been signed by Tsui
Chien Ngo appeared in the same paper on August 15,
1939.

Taken by surprise of the appearance of the
letters in the Sin Shun Pao, both Chen and Tsui
tried to alleviate public antagonism by publishing
an announcement in local vernacular newspapers to
the effect that they are devoting their attention
to the promotion of education and have never issued
any circular letter. Their announcements, however,
neither deny nor confirm their support for Wang Ching
Wei.

Since the appearance of the letters in the
Sin Shun Pao, both Chen and Tsui have failed to attend
their schools regularly due to fear of possible
repercussions from their students.

At about 11.30 a.m., August 22, some 8 or
9 Chinese youths called at the Shanghai Middle School,
460 Chengtu Road, and demanded to see Chen Chi-zung.
Failing to obtain an interview with Chen who was
absent, they caught hold of Chow Zu Tsoh (周汝作),
Dean of the school, and after slapping his face and
striking him about the body with stools, made good
their escape.

It is reported that Chen Chi-zung consulted
with Li Shih Chung (李自群), Assistant Director
page_data.zh:
(4)

1939年8月13日，《新顺报》上突然刊登了一封据称由陈继曾签署的支持汪氏和平运动的信件，而另一封据称由崔坚吾签署的类似信件于1939年8月15日出现在同一报纸上。

陈继曾和崔坚吾对信件出现在《新顺报》上感到措手不及，试图通过在本地中文报纸上发布公告来缓解公众的敌意，公告大意是他们致力于促进教育，从未发布任何通函。然而，他们的公告既未否认也未确认对汪精卫的支持。

自《新顺报》刊登信件以来，由于担心学生可能产生的反响，陈继曾和崔坚吾均未正常到校履职。

8月22日上午11时30分左右，约八九名中国青年前往成都路460号的上海中学，要求见陈继曾。因陈继曾不在，他们未能与其会面，便抓住该校教务主任周汝作，在扇其耳光并用凳子殴打其身体后，迅速逃离现场。

据报道，陈继曾就当天在其学校发生的事件，于8月22日咨询了汪精卫派系特务处副处长李自群，该特务处以“中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队”的名义活动。李告诉他，如果再次发生此类事件或学生中出现煽动行为，应将责任人和头目报告给李，李将通过日本宪兵以共产主义和反日挑衅的罪名实施逮捕。

page_data.en:
(5)

of the Secret Service of Wang Ching Wei's clique,
operating under the name of Special Service Corps
of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and
National Salvation Army, on August 22 with regard
to the incident which occurred in his school the
same day. He was told by Li that should any
further incidents of that nature or agitation
among the students arise, the responsible culprits
and ringleaders should be reported to Li who would
effect their arrest through the Japanese Military
Police on charges of communism and anti-Japanese
provocation.

According to information obtained from a
reliable source, the recent activities of these
persons have now come to the notice of the Chung-
king Government. Local agents of the Government
have secretly demanded a definite explanation from
them, especially Chen Chi-zung and Zi Tsuh-hsiang,
in order to clarify their attitude. While
Chen Chi-zung and the others are hesitating in
giving a definite reply, Zi Tsuh-hsiang has left
Shanghai for Hongkong en route to Chungking. Zi
was formerly a follower of Pan Kung Chai, ex-
chief of the Bureau of Social Affairs of the
Shanghai City Government in 1937 and is believed
to be still a secret agent of the National Govern-
ment posted in Shanghai to watch the activities
of the local educational circles.
page_data.zh:
(5)

据可靠消息来源获悉，这些人的近期活动已引起重庆政府的注意。政府的地方特工已秘密要求他们，特别是陈继曾和徐则驤，作出明确解释，以澄清其立场。当陈继曾等人犹豫不决，未给予明确答复时，徐则驤已离开上海前往香港，转赴重庆。徐曾是1937年上海市政府社会局局长潘公展的追随者，据信他仍是国民政府安插在上海监视当地教育界活动的秘密特工。

page_data.en:
(6)

The letter also alleges that Chen Chi Zung,
in conspiring with the Pan I Tai Rice Shop (潘義泰),
made a fortune by selling cereals to the "enemy" at
the time of the Mukden Incident and the Shanghai
Hostilities during 1932. This allegation lacks
confirmation, although Chen is known to be a good
friend of Pan Seu Zung (潘守仁), the proprietor
of the Rice Shop in question.

"The Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation
Federation" (上海市各团体救国联合会), the
title appearing at the bottom of the letter, is unknown
to this office. According to the record, there was a
body named Shanghai Various Circles Committee to support
Resistance Against the Enemy (上海市各界抗敌
后援会) which played a very important part in the
national salvation movement in Shanghai in the latter
part of 1937 but was closed down by the Municipal Police
on November 18, 1937. Since then, members of this
Committee, numbering over 100 and consisting of people
of various walks of life, have disintegrated to such
an extent that some of them have even turned against
the National Government. Discreet enquiries among all
possible sources have failed to elicit any trace of
this organization.

The address, 1317 Haining Road, given on the
envelope of the letter is located on Haining Road to
the west of the S.M.C. Boundary Gate on Haining Road
page_data.zh:
(6)

该信还指控陈继曾在“九一八”事变和1932年上海战事期间，与潘义泰米店合谋，通过向“敌人”出售谷物大发横财。这一指控缺乏证实，尽管众所周知陈继曾是该米店店主潘守仁的好友。

信末署名的“上海市各团体救国联合会”为本局所不知。根据记录，曾有一个名为“上海市各界抗敌后援会”的组织，在1937年下半年上海的救国运动中发挥了非常重要的作用，但该组织于1937年11月18日被警务处查封。此后，该委员会成员逾百人，涵盖各界人士，已分崩离析，其中一些人甚至转而反对国民政府。经向所有可能的来源进行谨慎查询，未发现该组织的任何踪迹。

信封上给出的地址海宁路1317号，位于海宁路工部局边界门以西，

page_data.en:
(7)

and at present inaccessible to persons from the Settlement being under the Japanese Naval Landing Party jurisdiction and it is therefore impossible to ascertain the occupants of this house.

The postal cancellation chops on the envelopes are illegible. A close study of the obscure impressions seems to indicate that they were posted at the General Post Office, North Szechuen Road, at about 11 p.m., August 18, 1939.
page_data.zh:
(7)

目前处于日本海军陆战队管辖之下，租界人士无法进入，因此无法查明该房屋的居住者。

信封上的邮戳模糊不清。仔细研究这些模糊的痕迹似乎表明，它们是在1939年8月18日晚上11点左右在北四川路邮政总局寄出的。

page_data.en:
Summary of the past activities of Chen Chi-zung

Chen Chi-zung (  ), principal of the
Shanghai Private Middle School, 460 Changtu Road, who is
residing at No.3/179 Connaught Road, was born in 1894 at
Kading, Kiangsu, and is a graduate of the Lungmen Normal
School, Nantao. After graduation, he obtained employment
in the Shanghai Cotton and Cotton Yarn Exchange, Avenue
Edward VII, as assistant Chief of the Business Section of
the General Affairs Department, and consequently met
Mr. Wen Lai Ding (  ), prominent local business man,
who was the chairman of the Board of Directors of the
Shanghai Cotton and Cotton Yarn Exchange. It is reported
that he is now one of Wen's followers.

In 1924, Chen Chi-zung, with financial assistance
from Wen Lai Ding, established the Shanghai Primary School
on Li Yuan Road, Nantao, and later established three more
primary schools under the same title at 1297 Robison Road,
No.2 Tsih Woo Fang, Rue de l'Ouest, and 400 Foochow Road.
In 1927 he established the "Shanghai Private Middle School"
in Pan's Garden, corner of Kinchow and Pingliang Roads and
also a kindergarten in the Kong Fong Li Alleyway (康芳里 ),
Connaught Road. Shortly after the outbreak of the local
hostilities in August, 1937, he had all his schools removed
to their present address, 460 Changtu Road, where he
conducts an elementary normal school, a middle school, a
primary school, and a kindergarten with a total of more than
4,000 students.

About the same time as he started this educational
work, he took an interest in the affairs of the Society and
participated in the activities of the 9th Branch of the 1st
Special District Citizens' Federation (156 Burkill Road).
His educational work and his connections with the Citizens'
page_data.zh:
陈继曾过往活动摘要

陈继曾（  ），成都路460号上海私立中学校长，居住于康纳脱路179号3室，1894年生于江苏嘉定，毕业于南市龙门师范学校。毕业后，他在爱多亚路上海棉纱交易所任职，担任总务部业务科副科长，因此结识了当地著名商人、上海棉纱交易所董事会主席温赖定（音译）先生。据报道，他现在是温的追随者之一。

1924年，陈继曾在温赖定的资助下，在南市梨园路创办了上海小学，随后又在罗别根路1297号、西爱咸斯路积余坊2号以及福州路400号创办了三所同名小学。1927年，他在锦州路与平凉路交界处的潘家花园创办了“上海私立中学”，并在康纳脱路康芳里弄堂创办了一所幼儿园。1937年8月本地战事爆发后不久，他将所有学校迁至现址成都路460号，在那里开办一所初级师范学校、一所中学、一所小学和一所幼儿园，学生总数超过4000人。

在他开始这项教育工作的大致同时，他对社会事务产生了兴趣，并参与了第一特区市民联合会第九分会（伯克路156号）的活动。他的教育工作以及与市民联

page_data.en:
- 2 -

ederation afforded him an opportunity to befriend local
prominent personages and gave him access to social circles,
afterwards being appointed an executive of the Chinese Rate-
payers' Association. In 1934 he was elected a Chinese
member of the S.M.C. for that year and since that date
his activities can be summarised as follows:-

Public Services

In the years 1934 and 1935, Chen Chi-zung was elected
to serve as the Chinese committee of the Shanghai Municipal
Council.

In 1936, he served as a member of the Advisory
Committee of the Shanghai Municipal Council.

On March 21, 1938, he was elected a Chinese Committee
member to the S.M.C. for the year 1938, which position he
resigned in November 1938.

On April 17, 1939, he was again elected at a general
meeting of the Chinese Rate-payers' Association to serve as
a Chinese Committee member to the S.M.C. for the year 1939.

For a number of years he has been a member of the
standing committee of the First Special District Citizens'
Federation, at present situated at No.545 Kiukiang Road.

Educational Activities

During the latter part of 1935, he served as a
committee member of the Shanghai Educational Association
(now defunct) in Nantao and also as a member of the Board of
Management of the Shanghai Middle School Teachers and Staff
Employees' Federation, then situated at 200 Dah Chih Road,
Nantao.

He is the Vice-Chairman of the Shanghai Children's
Protection and Education Association, 451 Taku Road, which
came into existence on June 1938, during a meeting of its
principal promoters held in the Chinese Y.M.C.A., 125
Boulevard de Montigny, French Concession. The object of this
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

合会的联系为他提供了结交当地知名人士的机会，并使他能进入社交圈，随后被任命为华人纳税会执行委员。1934年，他当选为当年的工部局华董，自此以后，他的活动可概括如下：

公共服务

1934年和1935年，陈继曾当选为上海公共租界工部局华董。

1936年，他担任上海公共租界工部局咨询委员会委员。

1938年3月21日，他当选为1938年度工部局华董，并于1938年11月辞去该职。

1939年4月17日，他在华人纳税会全体会议上再次当选为1939年度工部局华董。

多年来，他一直是第一特区市民联合会常务委员会委员，该会现址为九江路545号。

教育活动

1935年下半年，他担任南市上海教育协会（现已解散）委员，以及当时位于南市大智路200号的上海中学教职员联合会管理委员会成员。

他是上海儿童保护教育协会的副主席，该协会位于大沽路451号，成立于1938年6月，其主要发起人在法租界蒙太尼路125号中华基督教青年会举行会议时成立。该协会的目标是

page_data.en:
- 3 -
association is the protection and education of Chinese
children who have otherwise no opportunity of attending
school, and in particular street urchins.
He is one of the executive committee members of the
Shanghai Chinese Private Schools' Association (上海私立学校
联合会), with a communication address at the Min Kuo Middle
School, Lane 289/1 Weihaiwei Road, which derived its
existence from the amalgamation of the Settlement Private
Middle and Primary Schools Association, formerly with offices
at the Dau Chung Middle School for Girls (道中女子中学),
628 Avenue Road, and the 2nd Special District Private School
Federation at Hwa Tung Middle School for Girls (华东女中一),
462 Avenue Joffre, following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in the Shanghai Areas in August 1937. This
organization in the middle of October, 1938, despatched a
letter to the Education Department of the S.M.C., requesting
that the quarterly grants-in-aid for Chinese educational
institutions be issued in cash instead of "Wei-wah" Cheques.
This request was later learned to have received the favourable
consideration of the Council.
On April 17, 1939, he was elected to serve as one of
the members of the executive committee of the Federation of
Principals of Primary Schools, which was organized by Chen
in 1930 in conjunction with others, but which has been
inactive until early this year when the promoters commenced
resuming their activities and intensifying their campaign of
organization.
He has been the Chairman of the Board of Directors of
the Shanghai Children's Educational Publication Society,
since its formation sometime in May 1938, with offices at
Lane 152, House No.7, Chengtu Road. The object of this
organization is the printing and publishing of educational
books and the supplying of stationery and books to school
page_data.zh:
- 3 -
该协会的宗旨是保护和教育那些否则没有机会入学的中国儿童，特别是街头流浪儿。
他是上海私立学校联合会执行委员会委员之一，通讯地址为威海卫路289弄1号民国中学。该联合会是由租界私立中小学联合会（原址为爱文义路628号道中女子中学）与第二特区私立学校联合会（原址为霞飞路462号华东女中一）在1937年8月上海地区中日战事爆发后合并而成。该组织于1938年10月中旬致函工部局教育处，请求将对中国教育机构的季度补助金以现金形式发放，而非“维华”支票。后获悉该请求已获公董局 favorable consideration（有利考虑/正面考量）。
1939年4月17日，他当选为小学校长联合会执行委员会委员之一。该联合会由陈氏与他人于1930年组建，但一直未开展活动，直到今年初发起人才开始恢复活动并加强组织工作。
自1938年5月某时成立以来，他一直担任上海儿童教育出版社董事会主席，社址在成都路152弄7号。该组织的宗旨是印刷和出版教育书籍，并以优惠价格向学校

page_data.en:
- 4 -
children at reduced rates.
Participation in Relief Work.
He has been officer-in-charge of the Food Supply
Section of the Shanghai Emergency Relief Committee, 1454
Avenue Edward VII, since the formal inauguration of the
committee following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in the Shanghai area in August 1937.
He was one of the promoters and concurrently a member
of the standing committee of the Shanghai Municipality
Distressed Children's Nursery (上海市救濟難童教養院), with
an office at 203 Rue Chapsal, which came into existence in
June 1938. When this organization was formally inaugurated
on September 10, 1938, in the premises of the Leh Zuan Sz
Temple ( 樂善寺 ), Lane 785, No.9, Avenue Joffre, he
was elected Director of the Nursery.
He is a member of the Standing Committee of the
"Entertainment and Radio Broadcasting Sub-Committee" of the
Citizens' Contribution and Radio Broadcasting Committee of
the Shanghai Refugee Relief Association, which was formally
inaugurated at a meeting held on February 16, 1939. The
office of this sub-committee is established in Room 414,
405 Kiangse Road, the object of which is to raise funds for
the relief of refugees by soliciting contributions through
broadcasting and entertainment.
He is a committee member of the "Fellow Countrymen's
Contribution Soliciting Committee" of the Shanghai Refugee
Relief Association, which was inaugurated on January 7, 1939,
in the Chinese Bankers' Club, 59 Hongkong Road; he is the
secretary of the Hading Fellow Countrymen's Association, 12
Rue du Consulat,
A speech bearing on the subject of refugee relief was
given by him in a propaganda campaign over local broadcasting
stations between December 26, 1938 and January 2, 1939.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -
儿童提供文具和书籍。
参与救济工作。
自1937年8月上海地区中日战事爆发后该委员会正式成立以來，他一直担任位于爱多亚路1454号的上海急赈委员会粮食供应科负责人。
他是上海市救济难童教养院的发起人之一，并兼任常务委员，院址在霞飞路203号，该院成立于1938年6月。当该组织于1938年9月10日在霞飞路785弄9号乐善寺内正式开幕时，他当选为教养院院长。
他是上海难民救济协会市民捐输及广播委员会“游艺及广播小组委员会”的常务委员，该小组委员会于1939年2月16日举行的会议上正式成立。该小组委员会办公室设在江西路405号414室，其宗旨是通过广播和游艺活动募捐，以救济难民。
他是上海难民救济协会“同乡捐输劝募委员会”的委员，该委员会于1939年1月7日在香港路59号中国银行家俱乐部成立；他是嘉定同乡会的秘书，会址在领事馆路12号，
在1938年12月26日至1939年1月2日期间，他在当地广播电台进行的宣传活动中发表了一篇关于难民救济的演讲。

page_data.en:
- 5 -
sponsored by the Citizens' Contribution Soliciting Committee,
Shanghai Refugee Relief Association, 93 Canton Road.
Participation in national salvation activities
On January 12, 1935, he delivered a speech at a
memorial meeting held in the Chamber of Commerce Building,
North Soochow Road in memory of the late Pan Hung Sung, who
was arrested and convicted for his part in the anti-Japanese
terroristic activities in the Settlement in 1932 but died
in 1934 shortly after his release from prison. In this
speech, he eulogized the life and work of the deceased
patriot.
In March 1937, he was appointed a committee member of
the Cultural Circles Suiyuan Bandit Suppression Campaign
Support Association, with offices at 500 Rue Lafayette,
while in May of that year, (1937) he interested himself in
the formation of the "South-West Border Affairs Association
(西南边事协会)", being a preparatory committee
member of the association, which came into existence on May
5, 1937 with an office at Room 620 Continental Emporium
Building, Nanking Road.
On October 9, 1938, when the "Shanghai Thrift Committee
for the Relief of Refugees" (上海救济难民节约委员会), with an
office at Room No.304, No.59 Hongkeng Road, was formally
inaugurated to an endeavour to persuade the people to be
thrifty and to contribute the money saved towards the relief
of refugees and wounded soldiers in the interior, he was
appointed as a standing committee member.
During October 1938, when students of the Private
Shanghai Middle School, of which Chen is the principal, were
engaged in soliciting contributions in various restaurants
in the International Settlement on behalf of the "Shanghai
Municipality Winter Clothing Collection Committee", he was
warned by the Municipal Police on October 12, that no solicit-
page_data.zh:
- 5 -
该活动由上海难民救济协会市民捐输劝募委员会主办，地址在广东路93号。
参与救国活动
1935年1月12日，他在北苏州路商会大楼举行的潘洪松追悼会上发表演讲。潘洪松因参与1932年在租界内的反日恐怖活动而被捕定罪，于1934年获释后不久去世。在这次演讲中，他颂扬了这位已故爱国者的生平与工作。
1937年3月，他被任命为文化界绥远剿匪后援会委员，会址在辣斐德路500号；同年（1937年）5月，他致力于组建“西南边事协会”，担任该协会筹备委员会委员，该协会于1937年5月5日成立，办事处设在南京路大陆商场大楼620室。
1938年10月9日，“上海救济难民节约委员会”正式成立，会址在香港路59号304室，旨在劝导民众节约，并将省下的钱款用于救济内地难民和伤兵，他被任命为常务委员。
1938年10月期间，陈氏任校长的上海私立中学学生代表“上海市冬衣征募委员会”在公共租界各家餐馆进行募捐时，市政警察于10月12日警告他，未经工部局批准，不得在租界内进行募捐，

page_data.en:
- 6 -
ing of contributions would be allowed in the Settlement
without the sanction of the S.M.C., and that all
unauthorised collectors would be arrested by the Police
when seen.
In the middle of April, 1939, Chen Chi-zung was
reported to have been in close contact with Mr. Doong Ying-
pah (董英柏), a committee member of the local branch
of the Kuomintang, who maintained close and successful
liaison with the Local Tangpu and the authorities of the
various local schools, for the purpose of spreading propa-
ganda following the announcement of the People's Spiritual
General Mobilization by General Chiang Kai-shek in the
middle of March, 1939. At the same time, he was alleged
to be serving as Member of the Standing Committee of the
General Association of the Shanghai Various Circles'
People's Spiritual Mobilization Association. In
consequence of his reported connection with this Association,
he was warned on May 1, 1939, at Police Headquarters against
participation in activities relating to the promotion of
the People's Spiritual General Mobilization Movement.
On the morning of June 4, 1939, the Shanghai Middle
School, in celebrating the 15th Anniversary of the establish-
ment of the institute, hoisted two Chinese national flags on
its premises despite the fact that Chen Chi-zung, the
principal, was warned by the police and promised that no
flags would be displayed on that occasion. The two flags
were later removed by the police without anything untoward
happening.
page_data.zh:
- 6 -
所有未经授权的募捐者一经发现将被警方逮捕。
1939年4月中旬，据报陈济宗与国民党地方支部委员董英柏先生保持密切联系，董英柏与当地党部及各地方学校当局保持着密切且成功的联络，目的是在蒋介石将军于1939年3月中旬宣布国民精神总动员后传播宣传。同时，据称他担任上海各界国民精神总动员总会常务委员。鉴于据报他与该协会有关联，他于1939年5月1日在警察总局受到警告，不得参与促进国民精神总动员运动的相关活动。
1939年6月4日上午，上海中学在庆祝建校15周年之际，尽管校长陈济宗已受到警方警告并承诺届时不悬挂旗帜，但仍在校内悬挂了两面中国国旗。随后警方将两面旗帜移除，未发生任何意外事件。

page_data.en:
September 11, 1939.
Afternoon Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News publishes the following two
letters:

CONDITIONS IN LOCAL EDUCATIONAL CIRCLES

On September 7 your paper published a letter
from one Zau (邵) exposing the disloyalty of Chow Fee-
chen (周斐成), principal of the Hwa Tung Middle School for
Girls (華東女子中學), who had also taken six headmasters of
primary Schools over to the other side. It is regrettable
that Zau did not mention the names of the six headmasters
and their schools.
According to my information, the six primary
school headmasters are Koo (顧), Zien (錢), Soo (蘇),
Kung (孔), Wang (王), and Za (查). Since their
surrender, they have been paid large amounts of subsidy.
It was arranged to make an expression of their gratitude
to their master on September 6 but when the time came,
only Zien and Za actually fulfilled their promise for Chow
Fee-chen, Koo, Soo, Kung and Wang failed to appear. The
puppet authorities, suspecting ulterior purpose in the
absence of the other five men, took Zien and Za to the
Japanese Gendarmerie for interrogation.
This is indeed a serious warning to disloyal
elements.
Li Tse-loong (呂子龍),
September 8.

Your paper has been exposing pro-Wang elements
in educational circles but failed to mention the three
most important persons in provincial schools who are
most actively engaged with Chow Vai-hai (周佛海). Here
are their names and a record of their activities:-
1) Chow Yueh-sin (周越辛), principal of the Kiangsu
Provincial Wusih Normal School (江蘇省立無錫師範學校) and of
the Changchow Middle School in Shanghai (常州中學校),
formerly Supervisor of Schools of the Kiangsu Provincial
Educational Department, is an intimate of Chow Vai-hai.
When Chow Vai-hai arrived at Shanghai with Wang
Ching-wei, Chow Yueh-sin was the first person to help
Chow Vai-hai to buy over schools. He is an important
member of the puppet Educational Committee and receives
a salary of $200 with $800 for expenses.
2) Tung Tse-sien (童致旋), principal of the Kiangsu
Provincial Soochow Middle School (江蘇省立蘇州中學) and
Supervisor of Schools of the Shanghai Office of the
Kiangsu Provincial Educational Department, is a
confederate of Chow Yueh-sin and Chow Vai-hai. He is
engaged solely in the work of seducing schools and
receives a salary of $200 with $800 for expenses.
3) Yang Tsen-yu (楊震宇), principal of the Kiangsu
Provincial Soochow Normal School for Girls (江蘇省立蘇州女子師範),
is an active element under Chow Vai-hai and member of
the puppet Educational Committee. He receives a
salary of $500 with $500 for expenses.
Yang Tse-sin (楊致莘),
September 8.

1939年9月11日。
下午译文。

《中美日报》刊登以下两封信：

本地教育界状况

贵报于9月7日刊登了一封署名为邵（Zau）的来信，揭露华东女子中学校长周斐成（Chow Fee-chen）的不忠行为，称其还拉拢了六位小学校长投敌。遗憾的是，邵未在信中提及这六位校长及其学校的姓名。
据我所知，这六位小学校长分别是顾（Koo）、钱（Zien）、苏（Soo）、孔（Kung）、王（Wang）和查（Za）。自他们投敌以来，已领取大量津贴。原定於9月6日向他们的头目表示感激，但届时只有钱和查实际履行了对周斐成的承诺，顾、苏、孔和王均未出席。伪政权怀疑其余五人缺席别有用心，便将钱和查带至日本宪兵队进行审讯。
这对不忠分子确实是一个严重的警告。
吕子龙（Li Tse-loong），
9月8日。

贵报一直在揭露教育界的亲汪分子，但未提及在省立学校中与周佛海（Chow Vai-hai）勾结最紧密、活动最积极的三个最重要人物。现将他们的姓名及活动记录列下：
1) 周越辛（Chow Yueh-sin），江苏省立无锡师范学校及上海常州中学校校长，前江苏省教育厅督学，是周佛海的亲信。当周佛海随汪精卫抵达上海时，周越辛是第一个帮助周佛海收买学校的人。他是伪教育委员会的重要成员，月薪200元，办公费800元。
2) 童致旋（Tung Tse-sien），江苏省立苏州中学校长兼江苏省教育厅上海办事处督学，是周越辛和周佛海的同伙。他专门从事诱骗学校的工作，月薪200元，办公费800元。
3) 杨震宇（Yang Tsen-yu），江苏省立苏州女子师范学校校长，是周佛海手下的活跃分子及伪教育委员会委员。月薪500元，办公费500元。
杨致莘（Yang Tse-sin），
9月8日。

September 7, 1939.
Afternoon Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News publishes the following two letters:

PRO-WANG CHING-WEI ELEMENTS AMONG EDUCATIONALISTS

To the editor,
Your paper is to be admired for exposing the corrupt pro-Wang Ching-wei elements among educational circles. Since the arrival of Wang Ching-wei in Shanghai, he has been doing his utmost to seduce educationalists. As a member of educational circles, I have also been approached by some persons but I have paid no heed to them. The person who approached me is also a member of local educational circles; he stated that the following important educationalists have already joined Wang Ching-wei's party:-
1) Voong Yih-sien (馮一先), Principal of the Min Kuo Middle School for Girls (民國中學).
2) Tsan Chien-ngoo (崔堅吾), Principal of the Dao Tsung Middle School for Girls (道中女中).
3) Koo Che-wu (顧哲武), Principal of the Tsin Nien Middle School (青年中學).
4) Hwang Mei-yung (黃美雲), Principal of the Pootung Middle School (浦東中學).
5) Chow Loh-shan (周樂山), Chief Instructor of the Kwang Hsia Middle School (光夏中學).
6) Chang Yih-sung (張乙聲), Principal of the Jao Kwang Middle School (肇光中學).
7) Sung Yoh-zai (孫育才), Secretary and Acting Principal of the Tung Nan Middle School (東南職業學校).
I made an investigation and found his statement true. I therefore request the pro-puppet principals to give a definite reply so that the students of their schools may be saved from a slavish education.
Wang Jih-yung (黃日榮).

More Names of the Corrupt Elements

To the editor,
A grave warning has been given to local educational circles by your paper's exposure of Chen Chi-zung's (陳濟成) traitorous acts, but there are many other corrupt elements in educational circles, the most notorious of whom are the following for they attended the puppet National Congress of the Chinese Kuomintang:-
1) Tsa Hung-dien (蔡虹田), teacher in the Min Lih Middle School for Girls (民立女中) and chief attendant at the puppet congress.
2) Voong Yih-sien (馮一先), Principal of the Min Kuo Middle School for Girls.
3) Chang Zoong-kwei (張仲寰), Principal of the Sing Kwei Vocational School (新寰職校) and concurrently Dean of the Shanghai Middle School (上海中學).
Others are Ling Hsien-wen (凌憲文), Chin Kwan-mei (金關楣), Chang Yung-tsum (張泳春) and Tang Tsen-hwa (湯增敏) who are all in receipt of monthly subsidies from the puppet authorities.
All these corrupt elements are misleading the young men and doing harm to the nation and the race.
I am writing this to expose these people and if you would write articles attacking Tsa, Voong etc. as you have done with regard to Chen Chi-zung, it will be of benefit to the thousands of youths in Shanghai as well as to the Chinese race.
Li Choh-tse (李卓之).

1939年9月7日。
下午译文。

《中美日报》刊登以下两封信：

教育界中的亲汪精卫分子

致编辑：
贵报揭露教育界中腐败的亲汪精卫分子，令人钦佩。自汪精卫抵达上海以来，他一直极力诱骗教育工作者。作为教育界的一员，我也曾受到某些人的拉拢，但我未予理会。接触我的人也是本地教育界成员；他声称以下重要教育家已加入汪精卫的党派：-
1) 馮一先 (Voong Yih-sien)，民國中學校长。
2) 崔堅吾 (Tsan Chien-ngoo)，道中女中校长。
3) 顧哲武 (Koo Che-wu)，青年中學校长。
4) 黃美雲 (Hwang Mei-yung)，浦東中學校长。
5) 周樂山 (Chow Loh-shan)，光夏中學主任教员。
6) 張乙聲 (Chang Yih-sung)，肇光中學校长。
7) 孫育才 (Sung Yoh-zai)，東南職業學校秘书兼代理校长。
我经过调查，发现其陈述属实。因此，我要求这些傀儡校长给予明确答复，以便使各校学生免受奴化教育之害。
黃日榮 (Wang Jih-yung)。

更多腐败分子名单

致编辑：
贵报揭露陈济成 (Chen Chi-zung) 的叛国行径，已向本地教育界发出严重警告，但教育界中还有许多其他腐败分子，其中最臭名昭著的是以下几位，因为他们参加了伪中国国民党全国代表大会：-
1) 蔡虹田 (Tsa Hung-dien)，民立女中教师，伪大会主要随员。
2) 馮一先 (Voong Yih-sien)，民國中學校长。
3) 張仲寰 (Chang Zoong-kwei)，新寰職校校长，兼任上海中學教务长。
其他人包括凌憲文 (Ling Hsien-wen)、金關楣 (Chin Kwan-mei)、張泳春 (Chang Yung-tsum) 和湯增敏 (Tang Tsen-hwa)，他们均按月领取伪当局的津贴。
所有这些腐败分子都在误导青年，危害国家和民族。
我写此信是为了揭露这些人，如果您能像对待陈济成那样撰写文章抨击蔡、冯等人，将对上海成千上万的青年以及中华民族大有裨益。
李卓之 (Li Choh-tse)。

Chinese-American Daily News (Chungking telegram): 4.9.39/8
THE AFFAIRS OF THE SHANGHAI MIDDLE SCHOOL

Since the report on the disloyalty of Chen Chi-zung
(陳濟成), Principal of the Shanghai Middle School (上海
中學), and others, various quarters have paid close
attention to the matter.
The Ministry of Education of the Chungking Government
has received many telegrams from the people in Shanghai
requesting that punishment be imposed upon elements surrender-
ing to rebels and for withdrawal of the registration of the
schools concerned. The Ministry is making a close investi-
gation, and as soon as the report is found to be true,
punishment will be meted out to the persons concerned
immediately.
page_data.zh:
《中美日报》（重庆电报）：1939年9月4日/8
上海中學事件

自从报道上海中學 (Shanghai Middle School) 校长陈济成 (Chen Chi-zung) 及其他人的不忠行为以来，各方对此事给予了密切关注。
重庆政府教育部收到许多来自上海民众的电报，要求惩处投降叛逆的分子，并撤销相关学校的注册资格。教育部正在进行严密调查，一旦报告证实属实，将立即对有关人员予以惩处。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Misc. File No. 339/39
Chengtu Road Station,
REPORT
Date Sept. 28 1939.
Subject Reported dissension between Principal and Students of the Shanghai
Girls' University, 451 Taku Road.
Made by D. I. HILL Forwarded by [Signature]
Officer i/c.

Sir,
I beg to report that at 4.40 p.m. on the 26-9-39,
a telephone message was received from one Woo Ts Chih
(吴稚晖), Principal of the Shanghai Girls' University,
No. 451 Taku Road to the effect that he had received
a threatening letter and had arrested a suspect. In
response to the message received, P.C. 192 and P.C.
239 attended and brought complainant and suspect to the
station, the former produced a letter which he stated was
given to his private ricksha coolie by an unknown person,
on the 24-9-39, the coolie handed same to the principal
Woo Ts Chih to whom it was addressed, a translation of
the letter reads as follows:-

Sir,
We beg to inform you that recently rumour is
current outside to the effect that our mother
school will be purchased over by Wang's party.
While amazing at the news, we did retort this
rumour but without result.

Our mother school has had its glorious story
and if this rumour later proves true, will we
not be heart-stricken?.

We believe you will never do this and instead
you will still stick to your original policy so
as to bring about the ultimate victory.

However, rumour is horrible and we cannot
wait and see that you will not make an express
statement to refute the present existing rumour.

We therefore hereby request that on 27-9-39,
you insert an advertisement in the Sin Wan Pao
and Shup Pao expatiating on your attitude towards
our mother school and views re the rumour against
our mother school, thereby clarifying the outside
misunderstanding.

Trusting you will comply with our request
without recourse to resentment.
The High Middle School
Graduates of the current
term of this year.

（左侧手写批注：）
noted
SK Tan
4/9
S. S.
Cq
Lee Ch. Rd. Fk
13170

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
杂项档案号 339/39
成都路捕房，
报告
日期 1939年9月28日。
事由 据报大沽路451号上海女子大学校长与学生之间存在分歧。
制作人 D. I. HILL 转交人 [签名]
负责警官。

先生，
谨报告，1939年9月26日下午4时40分，接到大沽路451号上海女子大学校长吴稚晖 (Woo Ts Chih) 的电话留言，称其收到一封恐吓信并逮捕了一名嫌疑人。接到留言后，警员192号和警员239号前往现场，将报案人和嫌疑人带回捕房。报案人出示了一封信，称该信于1939年9月24日由一名不明身份的人交给他的私人黄包车夫，车夫随后将信交给了收件人校长吴稚晖。信件译文如下：-

先生，
特此告知，近期外界流传谣言，称我们的母校将被汪派收购。
听到这个消息我们感到震惊，虽曾反驳此谣言，但未见成效。

我们的母校有着光荣的历史，如果此谣言日后被证实为真，我们岂不痛心疾首？

我们相信您绝不会这样做，相反，您仍将坚持原有方针，以促成最终胜利。

然而，谣言可怕，我们不能坐视不管，希望您发表明确声明以驳斥目前存在的谣言。

因此，我们恳请您于1939年9月27日在《新闻报》和《申报》上刊登广告，阐述您对母校的态度及针对有关母校谣言的看法，从而澄清外界的误解。

相信您会遵从我们的请求，勿生怨怼。
本届高中
应届毕业生。

（左侧手写批注：）
已阅
SK Tan
9月4日
S. S.
Cq
Lee Ch. Rd. Fk
13170

On the 25-8-39, the suspect Tsiang Tsuh ( ),
age 16, female, residing house no. 146, lane 714 Yates
Road, student of the Shanghai Girls' School, handed the
principal a letter addressed to the latter, which she
claims was handed to her by her colleagues, a transla-
tion of the letter reads as follows:-
Sir,
We are afraid to say that you may be somewhat
astonished upon receipt of this letter, for it
comes to you too unexpectedly. We have first to
explain to you that this letter was written and
sent to you principally in view of the some 400
students and the future of our entire educational
work as well as the war of resistance and such an
action we deem to be correct.
Since the national army retreated from Shang-
hai, the inhabitants remaining on this isolated
island have been confronting with extreme diffi-
culties. However, it is worthy to be praised by
the whole nation and worshiped by the foreign na-
tionals that regardless of the hardship inflicted
on the inhabitants, all have come to stand on the
same line of which our educational walk is the
head. With this good sign in view, the recons-
truction of China during the period of war is sure
to be accomplished; yet the enormous errand mainly
rests on the educational walk, and we believe the
good educational walk will certainly stand up to
shoulder the errand.
Nevertheless, we realize, it is unavoidable
that before an event could be well accomplished,
failures may and will instantly be seen, particu-
larly, through the stirring of ill-feeling and
spreading of rumours by bad elements.
During the recent half year, a small number
of our educationalists have changed their minds
following the temptation and menace by shameless
fellows who came in contact with them, and instead
they, likewise stirred ill-feeling and spread
rumours from one school to the other and our school
is also one to be insulted. Our school, though a
private one, is known by the society for its
amicableness between the teachers and the students
and its consolidation of spirit. Though the evil
tiding came with surprise, we believe it was un-
reliable, for we still remember the remark made by

1939年8月25日，嫌疑人蒋祖 (Tsiang Tsuh)（ ），女，16岁，住耶茨路714弄146号，上海女子学校学生，向校长递交了一封写给后者的信，她声称这封信是她的同学交给她的。信件译文如下：
先生，
恐怕您收到此信会有些惊讶，因为它来得太突然了。我们首先要向您解释，写这封信并寄给您，主要是考虑到约400名学生、我们整个教育事业的未来以及抗战大局，我们认为此举是正确的。
自从国军撤离上海以来，留在这座孤岛上的居民一直面临着极大的困难。然而，尽管居民遭受苦难，所有人都站在同一条战线上，而我们的教育事业位居前列，这一点值得全国赞扬，也令外侨敬佩。鉴于这一良好迹象，战时中国的重建定能完成；然而，这项艰巨的任务主要落在教育界肩上，我们相信优秀的教育界一定能挺身而出，承担此重任。
尽管如此，我们认识到，在一件事圆满完成之前，失败可能会且确实会立即出现，特别是由于坏分子的煽动恶意和散布谣言。
在近半年来，少数教育家因受到无耻之徒的诱惑和威胁而改变了想法，这些人接触了他们，而他们也同样在各校之间煽动恶意、散布谣言，我们学校也受到了侮辱。我们学校虽是私立学校，但因师生和睦、精神团结而为社会所知。虽然噩耗来得突然，但我们认为其不可靠，因为我们仍记得您所说的

you that "The head could be chopped off but the will could never be softened". In order to make the society to have a clear viewpoint and to make the school-mates to more believe our school, we are obliged to make the following demands:-

1. No rectification of textbooks.

2. Freedom be given to social movements, such as hoisting of flag, morning exercise, opening of meetings, etc.

3. Protection be preserved for teachers and students' to love their school.

4. Speech unfavourable to the war of resistance be forbidden.

5. No grant-in-aid be received from irregular group.

6. Permission be first obtained from students in the event of duties being changed to a new teacher.

7. Testimonials be issued to schoolmates upon request.

8. Owing to high cost of living, tuition be paid monthly.

In connection with the above, you are hereby requested that your answer be explained in your reply and send each reply in print to the parents of the school-mates on the 26-8-39, in addition to which you are also requested to insert an advertisement in the Sin Van Pao and Shun Pao with strong words, thereby clarifying the outside misunderstanding, this must be done not later than 27-8-39. If you still linger on the matter, we will be sore in withdrawing from the school.

Finally we have to declare that we are not utilized or incited by any bad element.

SHANGHAI GIRLS' SCHOOL.
(Chopped) School-Protection Association.

Both letters were enclosed in a "buff" coloured envelope same being identical, the handwriting on the envelopes appears to be similar, but the letters were apparently written by different persons. No threats

“头可断，志不可屈”。为了让社会有清晰的观点，也让同学们更加信任我们的学校，我们被迫提出以下要求：-

1. 不修改教科书。

2. 给予社会运动自由，如升旗、晨操、召开会议等。

3. 保护师生爱校之情。

关于上述事项，恳请您在回复中加以解释，并于1939年8月26日将每份回复印刷后寄给学生家长。此外，还恳请您在《新闻报》和《申报》上用强烈的措辞刊登广告，从而澄清外界的误解，此事必须在1939年8月27日之前完成。如果您在此事上继续拖延，我们将悲痛地退学。

最后我们要声明，我们没有被任何坏分子利用或煽动。

上海女子学校。
（盖章）护校会。

Then was one of those students who tried to disturb the order and peace of the school.

She was quietly taken away and arrested and brought to the station where she was humiliated. Having known this information, all the students of this school requested their principal to accompany them to proceed to the police station, this was accordingly granted by him. Upon arrival at the station, and as a result of detective enquiries, the letter which was previously presented to the principal, "Woo", was proved to be without any threatening nature, thus the case was ordered to be withdrawn. At the station, the principal refused to express his sympathy with Mr. Wong Ching Wei, or having received any subsidies from Mr. Wong. Apart from the principal's own opinion towards Mr. Wong Ching Wei, we are consulting the fact that a student in Shanghai was unlawfully arrested and humiliated in the Police Station as a result of the principal's report, we are regretful that the education here should be deemed to be dangerous, hoping your paper will pay attention to this matter.

To the Editorial Dept.,
Chinese American Daily News.

Dear Sir,

Reference to the letter inserted in the educational and athletic section of the C.A.D.N. to the effect that I escorted a student by aid of handcuffs, I wish to point out that I have lately received a number of anonymous letters containing slanders, this being done as it will be seen, apparently with the subject of undermining the reputation of this school and of inciting strike in the school. In order to ascertain the truth, I am trying to locate the instigator.

At about 4 p.m. 25th August, an unofficial student of this school named Tsiang Tsuh presented me an anonymous letter, upon receipt of same, I notified the police station and when the detectives attended, I accompanied them to the station along with the letter-sender in order that the instigator might thus be implicated and later accordingly charged.

通过阅读吴先生寄来的信件，我们得知上海女子中学经常收到随意诽谤、损害学校声誉的匿名信；蒋素（Tsiang Tsuh，音译）被带往巡捕房，是因为她递交了一封无署名的匿名信，其内容无疑十分严重。根据昨天《中美日报》（S.A.D.N.）刊登的原信所述，蒋素呈交给吴先生的信是询问后者对汪精卫的态度。这确是事实，因为吴先生在回信中并未否认。根据同一封原信，蒋素被带往巡捕房后，负责调查的侦探阅读了原信，发现这纯粹是一封出于好意、旨在支持学校的信件，并非如校长所称的威胁信。案件没有结果。这也确是事实，因为吴先生也未予否认。我们希望向吴先生提出以下问题，同时也征求公众意见：

1. 仅因蒋素向吴先生递交了一封无署名、询问其对汪精卫态度的信件，吴先生将蒋素送往巡捕房是否值得？

2. 既然蒋素被送往巡捕房后案件仍无结果，吴先生对此作何感想？他是否会因此承担更多或更少的责任？

3. 最重要的问题是，吴先生是亲汪还是反汪？这不仅蒋素和上海女子中学的学生想知道，全中国人民也都期望知道。

吴先生能否就此作出明确声明？

Dear Sir,

I highly appreciate your publishing my letter
today.
Re queries raised, I answer them as follows:-

The S'hai Girls' School was inaugurated about
9 years ago, the school management is exercised
entirely in accordance with the laws of the national
government and the method of teaching is adopted
in a strict way.

In 1935, our school first started the "New
Life Movements" and petition to that effect was
presented to the Educational Bureau of the S'hai
Municipality and Order No. 26872 was given instruct-
ing the teaching staff and the students of this
chool to carry it on.

Following the outbreak of hostilities in 1937
our school sustained a heavy loss and still I am
loyal to the policy of the National Government and
obedient to the laws of the Board of Education.
I oppose whatever is detrimental to the National
policy and law, especially the speech made by Wang
Ching Wei who, kneeling on his thighs, is earnest
to acquire peace. I have made it known to my
teaching staff and students that "the head could
be chopped off but the will could never be softened".
Although the circumstances on the isolated island
are daily changeable, my confidence is still as firm
as a rock. Since our school was restored, cash
amounting to over ten thousand dollars had been
spent in purchasing equipments and, as it usual,
the meeting in memoration of the death of Dr. Sun
Yat-sen and the Students Self-control Association
etc. were carried out in addition to which flag was
hoisted in the morning, songs sung by teaching staff
and students during the hour the flag was hoisted
and lowered, all these can be proved by fact.

I have already anticipated that scandalous
persons will spread rumours thereby to keep us, who
are standing on the same line, from each other.
This undoubtedly affects a great deal to the future
of our education, nation etc.

Certain individual should be condemned to death
as also those of fractuating elements, but could

非常感谢贵报今日刊登我的来信。
针对所提问题，我回答如下：

上海女子中学创办于约9年前，学校管理完全依照国民政府法律执行，教学方法严格采用。

1935年，我校率先开展“新生活运动”，并向上海市教育局提交了相关申请，随后下达第26872号令，指示本校教职员工和学生推行该运动。

1937年战事爆发后，我校遭受重大损失，但我依然忠于国民政府政策，服从教育局法规。我反对任何有损国家政策及法律的行为，特别是汪精卫跪地求和平的言论。我已向教职员工和学生表明，“头可断，志不可屈”。虽然孤岛局势日新月异，但我的信心仍坚如磐石。自复校以来，已花费逾万美元购置设备，此外，照常举行了孙中山先生逝世纪念活动及学生自治会等活动，每日早晨升旗，升降旗期间由教职员工和学生歌唱，这些均有事实为证。

Chinese-American Daily News:-
Chen Chi-zung Elected Member-Elect of the Central
Supervisory Committee

Yesterday this paper reported that Chen
Chi-zung, Principal of the following four schools: the
Shanghai Middle School, the Shanghai Kindergarten Teachers'
Normal School, the Shanghai Primary School, and the Shanghai
Kindergarten, had been elected at the 6th National Congress
of the Chinese Kuomintang as member of the Central
Supervisory Committee.
According to reliable information from
foreign quarters, it is confirmed that Chen Chi-zung was
appointed "member-elect of the Central Supervisory Committee."
Chen is very much dejected over this
appointment for which he has sacrificed his reputation.

Yesterday many local educational and student
bodies sent telegrams to the Ministry of Education of the
National Government requesting it to punish Chen Chi-zung
and to cancel the registration of his four schools.
According to general belief, the four schools will not be
able to carry on for the fall term as there are now
less than 100 students.
page_data.zh:
《中美日报》：
陈济宗当选中央监察委员会候补委员

本报昨日报道，下列四所学校的校长——上海中学、上海幼稚园师范学校、上海小学和上海幼稚园——陈济宗，在中国国民党第六次全国代表大会上当选为中央监察委员会委员。
据外籍人士方面的可靠消息证实，陈济宗被任命为“中央监察委员会候补委员”。
陈济宗对这一牺牲其名誉的任命感到非常沮丧。

昨日，本地许多教育和学生团体致电国民政府教育部，要求惩处陈济宗，并注销其四所学校的注册资格。
普遍认为，这四所学校将无法继续秋季学期的教学，因为目前学生人数不足100人。

Chinese-American Daily News publishes the following letter
addressed to Messrs Yu Yo-ching, Yu-n Li-tung, Ling Kung-
hou and Vung Lai-ding :-

THE AFFAIRS OF THE SHANGHAI MIDDLE SCHOOL

Facts are to hand regarding the surrender
of Chen Chi-zung, who is the principal of the Shanghai
Middle and three other schools, who is supporting Wang
Ching-wei. All of you are directors of these four schools
and are admired for your enthusiasm in educational work.
You are probably in close touch with the situation in the
Shanghai Middle School, but up to the present, none of
you have said anything about the affair.
Advertisements of these schools bearing
your names are published in local newspapers. If the
students of the four schools who have confidence in you
decide to continue to study in these schools, then you
cannot avoid being blamed for doing harm to the students.
The Chinese-American Daily News on August 23
published a letter from a reader stating that the students
of the four schools have requested Chen Chi-zung to ask
the directors of the schools to explain the position of
the schools, but Chen replied that he could not do this.
This shows that Chen knows that he cannot mislead all
of you.
You have authority to deal with the affairs
of the four schools and it is your duty to supervise
the movements of the principal. The four schools are
about to re-open and I hope you will do something without
delay.

Tsung Li-ping ( 宗礼斌 ),
August 29, 1939.

上海中学事务

有关上海中学及其他三所学校校长陈济宗投降并支持汪精卫的事实已传到各位手中。你们都是这四所学校的董事，并以在教育工作的热情而受人钦佩。你们可能与上海中学的局势保持密切联系，但截至目前，你们中无人就此事件发表任何言论。
这些学校带有你们姓名的广告刊登在当地报纸上。如果信任你们的四所学校学生决定继续在这些学校就读，那么你们将无法避免因伤害学生而受到指责。
8月23日，《中美日报》刊登了一封读者来信，称四所学校的学生已请求陈济宗请学校董事解释学校的立场，但陈回答说做不到。这表明陈知道他无法误导你们所有人。
你们有权处理这四所学校的事务，监督校长的行动是你们的职责。四所学校即将重新开学，希望你们能立即采取行动。

宗礼斌（Tsung Li-ping），

THE AFFAIRS OF THE SHANGHAI MIDDLE SCHOOL FOR GIRLS

Urgent Notice Issued by Wu Tse-che

Wu Tse-che (吳志騫), the Principal of the Shanghai Middle School for Girls (上海女中), publishes the following urgent notice in the advertisement columns of the "Chinese-American Daily News" (中美日報) to-day:-
"I established the Shanghai Middle School for Girls nine years ago. I have given all my time to the affairs of the school in accordance with the laws and orders of the Ministry of Education of the Chungking Government and have taken no part in any political activities. I have faithfully observed the national policy of the Chungking Government and opposed all persons who act contrary to the national policy or to the laws and orders of the country. I strongly abhor Wang Ching-wei's peace proposals.
"Recently certain undesirable elements spread rumours harmful to my reputation and to the reputation of my school. Lest the public should be misled by these rumours, I hereby publish this notice for public information."

Chinese-American Daily News publishes the following letters from Wu Tse-che:

A Letter From Wu Tse-che

To the Editor,
On August 30 your paper published a letter addressed to me by one Tsung Li-ping (宗礼斌).
I am sending a reply to Mr. Tsung which I hope you will publish in your paper.
Wu Tse-che (August 30).

A Letter to Tsung Li-ping

To Mr. Tsung-Li-ping,
Your letter addressed to me in the "Chinese-American Daily News" on August 30 is noted, and I thank you very much for your concern about me.
I have clarified my attitude in a letter to the editor and in a notice published on the same day. Please examine them all and you will understand.
Wu Tse-che (August 30).

Chinese-American Daily News publishes the following article:

At midnight on August 29, this paper received a letter from Mr. Wu Tse-che (published in yesterday's paper), in which his attitude (as to whether he supports or opposes Wang Ching-wei) was clarified.
What we expect from Mr. Wu has now been done earnestly by Mr. Wu; we shall retain our confidence in Mr. Wu until facts prove his loyalty. For this reason, with the exception of the letter from Mr. Tsung Li-ping which we had published in our paper, all other articles we received that day dealing with the activities of Mr. Wu have been withheld publication for the time being.

上海女子中学事件

吴志骞发布的紧急通告

上海女子中学校长吴志骞（Wu Tse-che）今日在《中美日报》广告栏刊登如下紧急通告：
“本人于九年前创办上海女子中学。本人遵照重庆政府教育部之法令，全心致力于校务，未参与任何政治活动。本人忠实遵守重庆政府之国策，反对一切违背国策或国家法令之人。本人强烈憎恶汪精卫之和平提议。
“近期某些不良分子散布有损本人及本校声誉之谣言。为防止公众受此等谣言误导，特此发布本通告，以正视听。”

《中美日报》刊登吴志骞如下信件：

吴志骞来信

致编辑先生：
贵报于8月30日刊登了一封宗礼斌（Tsung Li-ping）致本人的信件。
现附上本人回复宗先生之信函，望贵报予以刊登。
吴志骞（8月30日）。

致宗礼斌函

致宗礼斌先生：
已阅阁下于8月30日在《中美日报》上致本人之信函，非常感谢阁下的关切。
本人已在同日致编辑的信函及通告中阐明了立场。请查阅上述文件，自会明白。
吴志骞（8月30日）。

《中美日报》刊登如下文章：

本报于8月29日午夜收到吴志骞先生一封信件（已刊登于昨日报纸），信中澄清了其立场（即支持还是反对汪精卫）。
吴先生现已认真做出了我们所期望之举；在事实证实其忠诚之前，我们将保留对吴先生的信任。因此，除我们已刊登的宗礼斌先生来信外，当日收到的其他涉及吴先生活动的文章均暂时扣发，不予刊登。

page_data.en:
This shows that our intention is only to maintain
a just stand. We have done this in Mr. Wu's case as we
shall do in the case of others.
Facts are stronger than arguments. It is better
to prove one's attitude by acts than by word or writing.
Mr. Wu certainly knows that the people throughout China,
especially the entire body of teachers and students of the
school established by him, are much concerned over his
attitude.

事实胜于雄辩。用行动而非言语或文字
来证明自己的态度更为可取。
吴先生肯定知道，全中国人民，
特别是由他创办的学校的全体师生，
都非常关注他的态度。

Subject Chen Chi Zung (陳濟成), Headmaster of the Shanghai Middle School - allegations contained in an anonymous letter addressed to the Shanghai Municipal Police.
Made by J. St. Tsai-liang Forwarded by C Gao
(See also D845.0521 (278-39))
On August 18th 1939, a letter in the form of an official declaration was received at Police Headquarters. This letter which bears the seal of an organization entitled "Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation Federation", alleges that Chen Chi-zung, principal of the Shanghai Middle School, 160 Chengtu Road, has allied himself with Wang Ching Wei's Clique and has been in receipt of subsidy from them. His duties, according to the letter, consist of exploiting teachers and students of local Chinese schools for the benefit of Wang's cause, conducting pro-Wang and anti-British propaganda, supplying the "enemy" with information on the military and political secrets of the National Government as well as the activities of the authorities of the Foreign Settlements at Shanghai.
Chen Chi-zung, native of Kading, Jiangsu, age 45, is a committee member of the Shanghai Municipal Council and lives at 3/179 Connaught Road. A summary of his past activities is appended to this report.
He is unscrupulous but smart. The record shows that in the past he was an ardent supporter of the national salvation movement and participated in all kinds of movements which would bring him before the public eye, but undoubtedly his real object has been to attain prominence in social as well as political circles so as to pave the way for his own

1939年8月18日，警务处总部收到一封形式为正式声明的信件。该信件盖有名为“上海各界救国联合会”组织的印章，指控成都路160号上海中学校长陈济成与汪精卫派系勾结，并接受其津贴。据该信称，其职责包括利用当地华校师生为汪氏事业谋利，进行亲汪反英宣传，向“敌人”提供国民政府的军事和政治机密以及上海外国租界当局的活动情报。
陈济成，江苏嘉定人，45岁，系上海工部局委员，居住于康纳特路（Connaught Road）179号3室。本报告附录为其过往活动摘要。
此人虽聪明但无原则。记录显示，他过去是救国运动的热情支持者，参与了各种能使其受到公众关注的运动，但无疑其真实目的是在社会及政治圈中获得显赫地位，从而为其自身

Through his position as principal of a school
having more than 1,000 students, he succeeded in
attracting the attention of the local Chinese community
in 1936. His ardour in national salvation movements
following the outbreak of the local Sino-Japanese
hostilities in 1937, gradually turned the attention
into respect and won over the confidence and support
of the Chinese people.

Consequently, at the beginning of June, 1939,
when Wang Ching Wei's clique decided to undermine
General Chiang's influence in Shanghai through edu-
cational circles, Chow Yuh-hai (周佛海), right-
hand man of Wang in the peace movement, approached
Chen with handsome bribes. Chen succumbed and
in the middle of June, 1939 he succeeded in enlisting
the co-operation of six others and formed a committee
known as "Shanghai Educational Committee (上海教育
委員會)" also known as "Chung Kuo Kuomintang Edu-
cational Circles' Branch' (中國國民黨教育界支部)",
with Chen himself as the Chairman. Among the
six persons, four are known to be the following persons :-
Feng Ih-sien (一先), Principal of the Min
Kuo (民國) Middle School, 1/289

In turn for the appointment, they are said to have
etc. signed a pledge form supporting Wang Ching Wei's
cause. Chen's salary is $600 per month while
the other committee members receive $300 each monthly.
In addition a monthly sum of $5,000 has been granted
to the Committee for use in buying over the allegiance
of local middle and primary schools at the rate of
between $100 and $300 per month for middle schools
and between $50 and $80 for primary schools. It
is reported that up to the present time some 50
schools have joined Chen and thus benefited by this
money; the names of the schools however cannot be
ascertained at present.

Because of fear of reprisals from the Chung-
king Government the Committee have so far refused to
conduct the pro-Wang movement in the open, despite
repeated persuasion from their employers. The
latter insisted upon the former making public their
support of Wang's cause for the following reasons :-
to prevent the committee members from reverting in
future, to convince the public of the extent of Wang's
influence in Shanghai and to induce others to join.

Becoming impatient with the secretive
attitude of these followers, Wang's clique decided
to employ indirect methods to force their hands.

Suddenly on August 17, 1939 a letter alleged to
have been signed by Chen Chi Sung in support of Wang's
puppet government appeared in the Sin Shun Pao while
a similar letter alleged to have been signed by Tsui
Mien Ngo appeared in the same paper on August 18,
1939.

Taken by surprise of the appearance of the
letters in the Sin Shun Pao, both Chen and Tsui
tried to alleviate public antagonism by publishing
an announcement in local vernacular newspapers to
the effect that they are devoting their attention
to the promotion of education and have never issued
any circular letter. Their announcements, however,
neither deny nor confirm their support for Wang Ching
Wei.

Since the appearance of the letters in the
Sin Shun Pao, both Chen and Tsui have failed to attend
their schools regularly due to fear of possible
repercussions from their students.

At about 11.30 a.m., August 22, some 8 or
9 Chinese youths called at the Shanghai Middle School,
460 Chengtu Road, and demanded to see Chen Chi-zung.
Failing to obtain an interview with Chen who was
absent, they caught hold of Chow Zu Tsoh (周汝作),
Dean of the school, and after slapping his face and
striking him about the body with stools, made good
their escape.

It is reported that Chen Chi-zung consulted
with Li Shih Chung (李自群), Assistant Director

1939年8月17日，《新顺报》（Sin Shun Pao）突然刊登了一封据称由陈济成签署的支持汪氏傀儡政府的信件，而另一封据称由崔勉吾（Tsui Mien Ngo，即前文崔坚吾）签署的类似信件于1939年8月18日出现在同一报纸上。

陈济成和崔坚吾对信件出现在《新顺报》上感到措手不及，试图通过在本地白话报纸上发布公告来缓解公众的敌意，声称他们致力于促进教育，从未发布过任何通函。然而，他们的公告既未否认也未确认对汪精卫的支持。

自从《新顺报》刊登信件以来，由于担心学生可能产生的反响，陈济成和崔坚吾均未正常到校。

8月22日上午11时30分左右，约八九名中国青年前往成都路460号的上海中学，要求见陈济成。因陈济成不在，他们未能与其会面，便抓住该校教务长周汝作（Chow Zu Tsoh），扇其耳光并用凳子殴打其身体，随后逃离现场。

据报道，陈济成就当天发生在其学校的事件，于8月28日咨询了汪精卫派系特务处副处长李自群（Li Shih Chung），该特务处以“中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队”的名义活动。

The letter also alleges that Chen Chi Zung,
in conspiracy with the Pan I Tai Rice Shop (潘義泰),
made a fortune by selling cereals to the "enemy" at
the time of the Mukden Incident and the Shanghai
hostilities during 1937. This allegation lacks
confirmation, although Chen is known to be a good
friend of Ian Seu Zung (潘守仁), the proprietor

"The Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation
Federation" (上海市各團體救國聯合會), the
title appearing at the bottom of the letter, is unknown
to this office. According to the record, there was a
body named Shanghai Various Circles Committee to support
Resistance Against the Enemy (上海市各界抗敵
後援會) which played a very important part in the
national salvation movement in Shanghai in the latter
part of 1937 but was closed down by the Municipal Police
on November 13, 1937. Since then, members of this
Committee, numbering over 100 and consisting of people
of various walks of life, have disintegrated to such
an extent that some of them have even turned against
the National Government. Discreet enquiries among all
possible sources have failed to elicit any trace of
this organization.

The address, 1317 Haining Road, given on the
envelope of the letter is located on Haining Road to
the west of the S.M.C. Boundary Gate on Haining Road

page_data.en:
Summary of the past activities of Chen Chi-zung

Chen Chi-zung (陳濟成), principal of the
Shanghai Private Middle School, 460 Chengtu Road, who is
residing at No.3/179 Connaught Road, was born in 1894 at
Kading, Kiangsu, and is a graduate of the Lungmen Normal
School. Nantao. After graduation, he obtained employment
in the Shanghai Cotton and Cotton Yarn Exchange, Avenue
Edward VII, as assistant Chief of the Business Section of
the General Affairs Department, and consequently met
Mr. Wen Lai Ding (聞蘭亭), prominent local business man,
who was the chairman of the Board of Directors of the
Shanghai Cotton and Cotton Yarn Exchange. It is reported
that he is now one of Wen's followers.

In 1924, Chen Chi-zung, with financial assistance
from Wen Lai Ding, established the Shanghai Primary School
on Li Yuan Road, Nantao, and later established three more
primary schools under the same title at 1297 Robison Road,
No.2 Tsih Woo Fang, Rue de l'Ouest, and 400 Foochow Road.
In 1927 he established the "Shanghai Private Middle School"
in Pan's Garden, corner of Kinchow and Pingliang Roads and
also a kindergarten in the Kong Fong Li Alleyway (康芳里),
Connaught Road. Shortly after the outbreak of the local
hostilities in August, 1937, he had all his schools removed
to their present address, 460 Chengtu Road, where he
conducts an elementary normal school, a middle school, a
primary school, and a kindergarten with a total of more than
4,000 students.

About the same time as he started this educational
work, he took an interest in the affairs of the Society and
participated in the activities of the 9th Branch of the 1st
Special District Citizens' Federation (156 Burkill Road).
His educational work and his connections with the Citizens'
page_data.zh:
陈济成过往活动摘要

陈济成（陳濟成），成都路460号上海私立中学校长，现居住于康纳特路179弄3号，1894年出生于江苏嘉定，毕业于南市龙门师范学校。毕业后，他在爱多亚路上海棉纱交易所任职，担任总务部业务科副科长，从而结识了当地著名商人、上海棉纱交易所董事会主席闻兰亭（聞蘭亭）先生。据报道，他现在是闻的追随者之一。

1924年，陈济成在闻兰亭的资助下，在南市梨园路创办了上海小学，随后又在罗别根路1297号、西区第二织伍坊以及福州路400号创办了三所同名的初级小学。1927年，他在锦州路与平凉路交界处的潘家花园创办了“上海私立中学”，并在康纳特路康芳里弄堂创办了一所幼儿园。1937年8月本地战事爆发后不久，他将所有学校迁至目前的地址成都路460号，在那里他开办了一所初级师范学校、一所中学、一所小学和一所幼儿园，学生总数超过4,000人。

在他开始这项教育工作的大致同一时期，他对社会事务产生了兴趣，并参与了第一特区市民联合会第九分会（伯基尔路156号）的活动。他的教育工作以及与市民联

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Federation afforded him an opportunity to befriend local
prominent personages and gave him access to social circles,
afterwards being appointed an executive of the Chinese Rate-
payers' Association. In 1934 he was elected a Chinese
member of the S.M.C. for that year and since that date
his activities can be summarised as follows:-

Public Services

In the years 1934 and 1935, Chen Chi-zung was elected
to serve as the Chinese committee of the Shanghai Municipal
Council.

In 1936, he served as a member of the Advisory
Committee of the Shanghai Municipal Council.

On March 21, 1938, he was elected a Chinese Committee
member to the S.M.C. for the year 1938, which position he
resigned in November 1938.

On April 17, 1939, he was again elected at a general
meeting of the Chinese Rate-payers' Association to serve as
a Chinese Committee member to the S.M.C. for the year 1939.

For a number of years he has been a member of the
standing committee of the First Special District Citizens'
Federation, at present situated at No.545 Kiukiang Road.

Educational Activities

During the latter part of 1935, he served as a
committee member of the Shanghai Educational Association
(now defunct) in Nantao and also as a member of the Board of
Management of the Shanghai Middle School Teachers and Staff
Employees' Federation, then situated at 200 Dah Chih Road,
Nantao.

He is the Vice-Chairman of the Shanghai Children's
Protection and Education Association, 451 Taku Road, which
came into existence on June 1938, during a meeting of its
principal promoters held in the Chinese Y.M.C.A., 123
Boulevard de Montigny, French Concession. The object of this
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

合会的联系为他提供了结交当地知名人士的机会，并使他能进入社交圈，随后被任命为华人纳税会执行委员。1934年，他当选为当年工部局华董，自那时起，他的活动可概括如下：-

公共服务

1934年和1935年，陈济成当选为上海工部局华籍委员。

1936年，他担任上海工部局咨询委员会委员。

1938年3月21日，他当选为1938年度工部局华籍委员，并于1938年11月辞去该职。

1939年4月17日，他在华人纳税会全体会议上再次当选为1939年度工部局华籍委员。

多年来，他一直是第一特区市民联合会常务委员会委员，该会现址为九江路545号。

教育活动

1935年下半年，他担任南市上海教育协会（现已解散）委员，并担任当时位于南市大治路200号的上海中学教职员联合会管理委员会委员。

他是位于太古路451号的上海儿童保护教育协会的副主席，该协会于1938年6月在法租界蒙梯尼大道123号中华基督教青年会举行的主要发起人会议上成立。该

page_data.en:
- 3 -
association is the protection and education of Chinese
children who have otherwise no opportunity of attending
school, and in particular street urchins.
He is one of the executive committee members of the
Shanghai Chinese Private Schools' Association (上海私校
協進會), with a communication address at the Min Kuo Middle
School, Lane 289/1 Weihaiwei Road, which derived its
existence from the amalgamation of the Settlement Private
Middle and Primary Schools Association, formerly with offices
at the Dau Chung Middle School for Girls (道中女子中學),
628 Avenue Road, and the 2nd Special District Private School
Federation at Hwa Tung Middle School for Girls (華東女中學),
462 Avenue Joffre, following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in the Shanghai Areas in August 1937. This
organization in the middle of October, 1938, despatched a
letter to the Education Department of the S.M.C., requesting
that the quarterly grants-in-aid for Chinese educational
institutions be issued in cash instead of "Wei-wah" Cheques.
This request was later learned to have received the favourable
consideration of the Council.
On April 17, 1939, he was elected to serve as one of
the members of the executive committee of the Federation of
Principals of Primary Schools, which was organized by Chen
in 1930 in conjunction with others, but which has been
inactive until early this year when the promoters commenced
resuming their activities and intensifying their campaign of
organization.
He has been the Chairman of the Board of Directors of
the Shanghai Children's Educational Publication Society,
since its formation sometime in May 1938, with offices at
Lane 152, House No.7, Chengtu Road. The object of this
organization is the printing and publishing of educational
books and the supplying of stationery and books to school
page_data.zh:
- 3 -
协会的宗旨是保护和教育那些否则没有机会上学的中国儿童，特别是街头流浪儿。
他是上海私校协进会执行委员会委员之一，通讯地址为威海卫路289弄1号民国中学，该会是由租界私立中小学联合会（原办事处设在爱文义路628号道中女子中学）与第二特区私立学校联合会（原设在霞飞路462号华东女中学）在1937年8月上海地区中日战事爆发后合并而成。1938年10月中旬，该组织致函工部局学务处，请求将对华教机构的季度补助金以现金形式发放，而非“维华”支票。后获悉该请求已得到工部局的有利考虑。
1939年4月17日，他当选为小学校长联合会执行委员会委员之一，该联合会由陈于1930年与他人共同组织，但一直未开展活动，直到今年年初发起人才开始恢复活动并加强组织工作。
自1938年5月某时成立以来，他一直担任上海儿童教育出版社董事会主席，社址在成都路152弄7号。该组织的宗旨是印刷和出版教育书籍，并以优惠价格向学校

page_data.en:
- 4 -
children at reduced rates.
Participation in Relief Work.
He has been officer-in-charge of the Food Supply
Section of the Shanghai Emergency Relief Committee, 1454
Avenue Edward VII, since the formal inauguration of the
committee following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in the Shanghai area in August 1937.
He was one of the promoters and concurrently a member
of the standing committee of the Shanghai Municipality'
Distressed Children's Nursery (上海市救濟難童教養院), with
an office at 203 Rue Chapsal, which came into existence in
June 1938. When this organization was formally inaugurated
on September 10, 1938, in the premises of the Loh Zuan Sz
Temple ( 樂善寺 ), Lane 785, No.9, Avenue Joffre, he
was elected Director of the Nursery.
He is a member of the Standing Committee of the
"Entertainment and Radio Broadcasting Sub-Committee" of the
Citizens' Contribution and Radio Broadcasting Committee of
the Shanghai Refugee Relief Association, which was formally
inaugurated at a meeting held on February 16, 1939. The
office of this sub-committee is established in Room 414,
405 Kiangse Road, the object of which is to raise funds for
the relief of refugees by soliciting contributions through
broadcasting and entertainment.
He is a committee member of the "Fellow Countrymen's
Contribution Soliciting Committee" of the Shanghai Refugee
Relief Association, which was inaugurated on January 7, 1939,
in the Chinese Bankers' Club, 59 Hongkong Road; he is the
chairman of the Kading Fellow Countrymen's Association, 12
Rue du Consulat.
A speech bearing on the subject of refugee relief was
given by him in a propaganda campaign over local broadcasting
Stations between December 26, 1938 and January 2, 1939,
page_data.zh:
- 4 -
儿童供应文具和书籍。
参与救济工作。
自1937年8月上海地区中日战事爆发后该委员会正式成立以来，他一直担任位于爱多亚路1454号的上海急赈委员会粮食供应股主任。
他是上海市救济难童教养院（办公室设在夏泼萨尔路203号）的发起人之一兼常务委员，该院成立于1938年6月。当该组织于1938年9月10日在霞飞路785弄9号乐善寺（ 樂善寺 ） premises 正式开幕时，他当选为教养院院长。
他是上海难民救济协会市民捐输广播委员会“游艺广播小组委员会”常务委员，该小组委员会于1939年2月16日举行的会议上正式成立。该小组委员会办公室设在江西路405号414室，其宗旨是通过广播和游艺募捐，筹集资金救济难民。
他是上海难民救济协会“同乡捐输劝募委员会”委员，该委员会于1939年1月7日在香港路59号中国银行家俱乐部成立；他是位于领事馆路12号的嘉定同乡会主席。
1938年12月26日至1939年1月2日期间，他在由上海难民救济协会市民捐输劝募委员会（广东路93号）赞助的本地广播电台宣传活动中，发表了一篇关于难民救济主题的演讲，

page_data.en:
- 5 -
sponsored by the Citizens' Contribution Soliciting Committee,
Shanghai Refugee Relief Association, 93 Canton Road.
Participation in national salvation activities
On January 12, 1935, he delivered a speech at a
memorial meeting held in the Chamber of Commerce Building,
North Soochow Road in memory of the late Pan Hung Sung, who
was arrested and convicted for his part in the anti-Japanese
terroristic activities in the Settlement in 1932 but died
in 1934 shortly after his release from prison. In this
speech, he eulogized the life and work of the deceased
patriot.
In March 1937, he was appointed a committee member of
the Cultural Circles Spiyuan Bandit Suppression Campaign
Support Association, with offices at 500 Rue Lafayette,
while in May of that year, (1937) he interested himself in
the formation of the "South-West Border Affairs Association
(西南边疆事务会)", being a preparatory committee
member of the association, which came into existence on May
5, 1937 with an office at Room 620 Continental Emporium
Building, Nanking Road.
On October 9, 1938, when the "Shanghai Thrift Committee
for the Relief of Refugees" (上海救济难民节约
委员会), with an
office at Room No.304, No.59 Hongkong Road, was formally
inaugurated to an endeavour to persuade the people to be
thrifty and to contribute the money saved towards the relief
of refugees and wounded soldiers in the interior, he was
appointed as a standing committee member.
During October 1938, when students of the Private
Shanghai Middle School, of which Chen is the principal, were
engaged in soliciting contributions in various restaurants
in the International Settlement on behalf of the "Shanghai
Municipality Winter Clothing Collection Committee", he was
warned by the Municipal Police on October 12, that no solicit-
page_data.zh:
- 5 -
参与救国活动
1935年1月12日，他在北苏州路商会大楼举行的纪念潘鸿松逝世大会上发表演讲。潘鸿松因参与1932年在租界内的反日恐怖活动而被捕定罪，1934年获释后不久去世。在这次演讲中，他颂扬了这位已故爱国者的生平与工作。
1937年3月，他被任命为文化界绥远剿匪后援会委员，该会办公室设在拉斐德路500号；同年（1937年）5月，他致力于“西南边疆事务会”的组建，担任该会筹备委员，该会于1937年5月5日成立，办公室设在南京路大陆商场大楼620室。
1938年10月9日，“上海救济难民节约委员会”（办公室设在香港路59号304室）正式成立，旨在劝导民众节俭，并将省下的钱款捐赠给内地难民和伤兵，他被任命为常务委员。
1938年10月期间，当陈任校长的上海私立中学学生代表“上海市冬令寒衣征集委员会”在国际租界各家餐馆募捐时，工部局警务处于10月12日警告他，不得募集

page_data.en:
- 6 -
ing of contributions would be allowed in the Settlement
without the sanction of the S.M.C., and that all
unauthorised collectors would be arrested by the Police
when seen.
In the middle of April, 1939, Chen Chi-zung was
reported to have been in close contact with Mr. Doong Ying-
pah (董行白), a committee member of the local branch
of the Kuomintang, who maintained close and successful
liaison with the Local Tangpu and the authorities of the
various local schools, for the purpose of spreading propa-
ganda following the announcement of the People's Spiritual
General Mobilization by General Chiang Kai-shek in the
middle of March, 1939. At the same time, he was alleged
to be serving as Member of the Standing Committee of the
General Association of the Shanghai Various Circles'
People's Spiritual Mobilization Association. In
consequence of his reported connection with this Association,
he was warned on May 1, 1939, at Police Headquarters against
participation in activities relating to the promotion of
the People's Spiritual General Mobilization Movement.
On the morning of June 4, 1939, the Shanghai Middle
School, in celebrating the 15th Anniversary of the establish-
ment of the institute, hoisted two Chinese national flags on
its premises despite the fact that Chen Chi-sung, the
principal, was warned by the police and promised that no
flags would be displayed on that occasion. The two flags
were later removed by the police without anything untoward
happening.
page_data.zh:
- 6 -
未经工部局（S.M.C.）批准，不得在租界内进行募捐活动，所有未经授权的募捐者一经发现，即由警方逮捕。
1939年4月中旬，据报陈济成与国民党地方支部委员董行白先生（Mr. Doong Ying-pah）保持密切联系，后者与当地塘浦及各地方学校当局保持着密切且有效的联络，旨在传播宣传，响应蒋介石将军于1939年3月中旬宣布的“国民精神总动员”。同时，他被指担任上海各界国民精神总动员协会常务委员会委员。鉴于其与上述协会的所谓联系，他于1939年5月1日在警察总局受到警告，不得参与与推动国民精神总动员运动有关的活动。
1939年6月4日上午，上海中学在庆祝建校15周年之际，尽管校长陈济成已受警方警告并承诺届时不悬挂旗帜，该校仍在其校内悬挂了两面中国国旗。随后警方将这两面旗帜移除，期间未发生任何意外事件。

Translation of precis of anonymous
lette addressed to the Central Po-
lice Station.

Dated August 19, 1939.

Cher Chi Chen, Headmaster of the Shanghai Middle
School, member of the Executive Committee of the
Settlement Chinese Ratepayers Association and sponsor
of charity institutions, formerly made a fortune of
$700,000 by smuggling and selling cereals to the
"enemy" in association with owner of the Pan I T'ai
Rice Shop during "Mukden Incident" and Shanghai War
which broke out on January 28, 1932. As the govern-
ment did not punish him then he has become so bold
that he has committed the following offences, injurious
to the state and people:-

1. In order to obtain a sum of $16,000 monthly
as a grants-in-aid from the "enemy" he publicly sells
the students of 47 schools in Shanghai to the "enemy".

2. He issues publications and is engaged in pro-
paganda on behalf of the "enemy".

3. He allures patriotic youth to surrender them-
selves to the "enemy" by gain with a view to assisting
the "enemy" to achieve the work of aggression.

4. Taking advantage of his educational activities
he participates in the anti-British propaganda work in
order to impair the Sino-British friendly relations.

5. He acts as a spy for the "enemy" and receives
an allowance of $16,000.

As a member of the Ratepayers Association he fre-
quently keeps the "enemy" informed of the news of the
page_data.zh:
致中央捕房的匿名信摘要译文。

日期：1939年8月19日。

上海中学校长、公共租界华人纳税会执行委员会委员及慈善机构赞助人陈济成，曾在“九一八事变”及1932年1月28日爆发的上海战争期间，与潘义泰米店店主勾结，向“敌人”走私并出售谷物，从中获利70万美元。由于政府当时未予惩处，他变得如此大胆，犯下了以下危害国家和人民的罪行：

1. 为了每月从“敌人”处获得16,000美元的津贴，他公开将上海47所学校的学生出卖给“敌人”。

2. 他发行刊物，从事有利于“敌人”的宣传。

3. 他以利益诱惑爱国青年向“敌人”投降，旨在协助“敌人”实现侵略工作。

4. 他利用其教育活动之便，参与反英宣传工作，以损害中英友好关系。

5. 他充当“敌人”的间谍，并领取16,000美元的津贴。

作为纳税会成员，他经常向“敌人”通报

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Settlement authorities.

In view of the above offences he would have
been put to death by this association but for the
fear that peace and good order in the Settlement
might be endangered. The Central Station is there-
fore requested to take action against him or expel
him from the Settlement; otherwise he will be exe-
cuted by a man from this association with a view
to eliminating a traitor.

(Chop of): Shanghai Public Bodies National
Salvation Association.

No. 539.

Shanghai, August 18, 1939.

To the French Municipal Council,
Shanghai.

Dear Sirs,
Zung Tsi-zun (陳濟成) is the principal of the
Shanghai Middle School; he is also a committee member of
the Chinese Ratepayers Association of the International
Settlement and is one of the leaders in philanthropic circles.
In conspiracy with Pei Ni Tai (潘義泰米店), a rice
shop owner, Zung Tsi-zun took advantage of the Mukden Incident
and the January 28 Incident in 1932 (the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in Shanghai) to supply a large quantity of grain
to the enemy, thereby making a profit of more than $700,000.
As he has not been punished by the Government,
Zung has become bolder. Since the outbreak of the Sino-
Japanese hostilities in Shanghai in August, 1937, the traitor
Zung has not only supplied foodstuffs to the enemy, but he has
been using his high positions, his prestige and his social
influence to "sell" the Chinese race with the object of
enriching himself.
The following are some of the unlawful activities
carried out by Zung:-
1) As the principal of the Shanghai Middle School
Zung has certainly great influence in educational circles and
is in touch with several dozen schools in Shanghai. At
present he has publicly sold the students of 47 schools to
the enemy. Every month he receives from the enemy a subsidy
of $16,000.
2) He publishes reviews and other literature
constituting propaganda in favour of the enemy.
3) With the money he receives, he tempts poor
youths to submit to the enemy so that they may assist
page_data.zh:
上海，1939年8月18日。

致上海法公董局，
上海。

敬启者：
陈济成（Zung Tsi-zun）是上海中学校长；他也是国际租界华人纳税会委员，并在慈善界担任领导职务之一。
陈济成与米店老板潘义泰（Pei Ni Tai）勾结，利用九一八事变和1932年的一·二八事变（上海中日敌对行动），向敌人供应大量粮食，从而获利超过70万美元。
由于他未受到政府惩罚，陈氏变得更加大胆。自1937年8月上海中日敌对行动爆发以来，汉奸陈氏不仅向敌人提供食品，还利用其高位、声望和社会影响力，“出卖”中华民族，以达到自肥的目的。
以下是陈氏进行的一些非法活动：

Messieurs,

M. Sun Tsi Sun (陳濟成), directeur de
l'École secondaire Lan Hai" (上海中學), membre du
Comité de l'Association des Contribuables chinois de la
Concession internationale, et un des chefs des milieux
philanthropiques, avait, à l'occasion de l'incident de
Jiawen, et de l'incident du 28 janvier 1932 (hostilités
sino-japonaises de Shanghai): de connivence avec le patron
du magasin de riz T'ei Ki Tai (潘義泰米店), fourni
une grande quantité de céréales à l'ennemi, réalisant ainsi
plus de 700.000 de bénéfices. Mais, comme il n'a pas été
puni par le Gouvernement, il devient plus audacieux depuis
l'ouverture ces hostilités sino-japonaises à Shanghai en
août 1937, le traître Sun, non seulement fournit des vivres
à l'ennemi, mais encore profitant de ses hauts postes, de
son prestige et de son influence dans la société, tente de
"vendre" la Race Chinoise, pour pouvoir s'enrichir.

Ci-après, nous vous exposons les actes illicites
commis par Sun :

1) Étant actuellement directeur de l'École
secondaire Lan Hai, Sun a certainement une grande influence
dans les milieux pédagogiques et il est en rapport avec plu-
sieurs dizaines d'écoles de Shanghai; à l'heure actuelle,
il a vendu publiquement à l'ennemi les élèves de 47 écoles
en recevant chaque mois, de l'ennemi, une subvention de
$ 16.000.

2) Il publie des revues et autres imprimés
constituant une propagande en faveur de l'ennemi.

3) Avec des gains pécuniaires, il tente les
jeunes gens patriotiques à se soumettre à l'ennemi, pour
qu'ils aident celui-ci à triompher dans la guerre d'agression.

4) Profitant de ce qu'il est directeur d'une
école, il fait une propagande orale et écrite anti-britannique
tentant de nuire aux bonnes relations sino-anglaises.

5) Il se fait espion grâce à la place qu'il
occupe dans les milieux philanthropiques; il a recueilli et
fournit à l'ennemi, toutes les informations du Gouvernement
Chinois ayant un caractère militaire ou politique; comme
rémunération de ce service, il reçoit de l'ennemi une sub-
vention de $ 16.000 par mois.
page_data.zh:
诸位先生：

陈济成（Sun Tsi Sun）先生，系“兰海中学”（即上海中学）校长，公共租界华人纳税会委员，亦为慈善界领袖之一。在甲午事变及1932年1月28日事变（上海中日战事）期间，他与“潘义泰米店”老板串通，向敌方提供大量粮食，从中获利逾70万元。然而，由于未受政府惩处，自1937年8月上海中日战事爆发以来，该汉奸孙某愈发大胆，不仅向敌方供应粮秣，更凭借其高位、声望及社会影响力，企图“出卖”中华民族以谋取私利。

兹将孙某所犯非法行为列举如下：

1) 孙某现任兰海中学校长，在教育界颇具影响力，并与上海数十所学校保持联系；目前，他公然将47所学校的学生出卖给敌人，每月从敌人处领取津贴16,000元。

2) 他出版刊物及其他印刷品，进行亲敌宣传。

3) 他以金钱利益诱惑爱国青年投降敌人，协助敌人赢得侵略战争。

4) 他利用校长身份，进行口头和书面的反英宣传，企图破坏中英良好关系。

5) 他利用其在慈善界的地位充当间谍；收集并向敌方提供中国政府所有具有军事或政治性质的情报；作为此项服务的报酬，他每月从敌人处领取津贴16,000元。

page_data.en:
6) Profitant de ce qu'il est membre du comité
de l'Association des contribuables, il fournit souvent à
l'ennemi, toutes les informations émanant des autorités
des Concessions.

A la suite des enquêtes, nous avons constaté
que Sun a réellement commis les actes énumérés dans les six
paragraphes ci-dessus. Etant donné que ses actes gênent la
politique de résistance arrêtée par la Chine, compromet
les bonnes relations entre la Chine et les autres Pays,
favorise l'agression de l'ennemi, nous aurions vouloir le
punir nous-mêmes. Toutefois, en vue de maintenir la sécu-
rité dans les concessions, nous vous adressons tout d'abord
la présente lettre pour vous prier de bien vouloir faire
immédiatement le nécessaire ou ordonner l'expulsion de Sun;
sinon, nous nous verrons dans l'obligation de faire exécuter
notre sanction par nos gens, en vue de protéger la Chine.

Cachet : Fédération des différentes associa-
tions de Shanghai pour le salut
national.

经调查，我们证实孙某确实犯有上述六段所列之罪行。鉴于其行为妨碍中国既定的抵抗政策，损害中国与其他国家的良好关系，助长敌人的侵略气焰，我们本欲自行予以惩处。然而，为了维持租界内的安全，我们特致此函，恳请阁下立即采取必要措施或下令驱逐孙某；否则，我们将不得不由我方人员执行制裁，以保卫中国。

August 15, 1939. Morning Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News

REFUTATION OF A "SIN SHUN PAO" REPORT

On August 13, the "Sin Shun Pao" published an article written by Chen Chi-zung (陳濟成), a member of the S.M.C. Educational Committee and Principal of the Shanghai Middle School (上海中學), announcing that he, together with the entire body of 4,000 students of his school, is whole-heartedly supporting the peace movement advocated by Wang Ching-wei.

After the publication of this article, various circles were greatly shocked, for Mr. Chen occupies an influential position in society and is active in social work.

A reporter of this paper yesterday had a talk with Mr. Chen over the telephone to ascertain the facts. He strongly denied the report, stating that he would publish a refutation in the newspapers. He added that during the past few years he had been engaged in education and charitable work and had never issued any telegrams or articles. Mr. Chen believes that the report might have been published by some member of educational circles with the object of undermining his reputation and influence.

An advertisement to this effect is published by Chen Chi-zung in to-day's "Sin Wan Pao" and "Shun Pao."

1939年8月15日。上午译文。

《中美日报》

驳斥《新顺报》一则报道

8月13日，《新顺报》刊登了一篇由工部局教育委员会委员兼上海中学（上海中學）校长陈济成（Chen Chi-zung）撰写的文章，宣布他与其全校4000名学生全心全意支持汪精卫倡导的和平运动。

文章发表后，各界大为震惊，因为陈先生在社会上占有重要地位，且积极参与社会工作。

本报记者昨日通过电话与陈先生交谈，以核实事实。他强烈否认该报道，并表示将在报纸上发表辟谣声明。他补充说，过去几年他一直从事教育和慈善工作，从未发布过任何电报或文章。陈先生认为，该报道可能是教育界某些人士为了破坏他的声誉和影响力而发布的。

陈济成在今日的《新闻报》和《申报》上刊登了与此相关的广告。

page_data.en:
Chinese-American Daily News (Chungking telegram) :-

CORRUPT EDUCATIONAL ELEMENTS BOUGHT OVER BY WANG CHING-WEI

According to secret information secured
by the Chinese authorities here, a few corrupt elements
among educational circles in Shanghai have been bought
over by the followers of Wang Ching-wei and have established
an Educational Committee. Persons are being despatched to
fabricate misleading reports in the hope of inducing
other educationists to join the Committee. Discreet
enquiries are being made into the names of these elements;
suppressive measures will be adopted against them.

Chinese-American Daily News :-

Wang's Followers Active in Shanghai

With a view to forming an executive body
to accelerate the establishment of a puppet government,
Wang Ching-wei has detailed many of his followers to
Shanghai to buy over weak-minded elements to work for him.
A so-called Shanghai Municipality
Educational Committee has been established but owing to
the loyalty of local educationalists towards the Kuomintang
and the Government, the Committee has found it difficult
to carry out its plans since its inauguration a little
over a month ago. It is said that the Committee will soon
be dissolved.
With the removal of all schools from the
occupied areas, Shanghai has now become the educational
and cultural centre of south-east China. Chow Vai-hai
(周佛海) and Ting Muh-tsung (丁默邨) are active among
educational circles in Shanghai. Prior to the hostilities,
Chow Vai-hai was at one time Commissioner of the Educational
Department of the Kiangsu Provincial Government, while
Ting Muh-tsung was formerly President of the Kiangnan
College (江南学院). Consequently, both of them are familiar
with educational circles in Kiangsu Province and in
Shanghai. To facilitate their work, this Committee was
established. It has a General Office with eleven members,
one of them serving as Chief. The Chairman of the
Committee is paid a salary of $600 a month, in addition to
a monthly liaison allowance of $2,000, while the Committee-
men are paid $300 each and the members of the General Office
$100 a month each. It is said that a certain educational
officer of the former Shanghai City Government, who is at
present unemployed, has been bought over and given the post
of Chairman of the Committee.

It is also said that the employees of the
Committee, prior to their assumption of posts, were all
required to take an oath and to pledge their support to
Wang Ching-wei.
The members of the Committee have requested
various schools to support the peace movement and are
offering a sum of $50 to every school which affixed its
chop on the printed form issued by the Committee, but all
these activities have resulted in failure. Moreover, due
to internal dissension among the members of the Committee
as well as to unequal distribution of profits, a serious
split has occurred and the Committee will probably be
dissolved before long.
page_data.zh:
《中美日报》（重庆电）：

汪精卫收买教育界败类

据此地中国当局获得的秘密消息，上海教育界少数败类已被汪精卫追随者收买，并成立了一个教育委员会。他们正派人编造误导性报道，希望诱使其他教育家加入该委员会。目前正在谨慎调查这些人的姓名；并将对他们采取压制措施。

《中美日报》：

汪氏追随者在上海活动活跃

为了组建一个加速建立傀儡政府的执行机构，汪精卫已派遣许多追随者前往上海，收买意志薄弱者为其效力。一个所谓的上海市教育委员会已经成立，但由于当地教育家对国民党和政府的忠诚，该委员会自一个多月前成立以来，一直难以实施其计划。据悉，该委员会不久将被解散。

随着所有学校从占领区撤出，上海现已成为中国东南部的教育和文化中心。周佛海（Chow Vai-hai）和丁默邨（Ting Muh-tsung）在上海教育界活动频繁。战前，周佛海曾担任江苏省政府教育厅厅长，而丁默邨曾任江南学院（江南学院）院长。因此，两人均熟悉江苏省和上海的教育界。为了方便工作，成立了该委员会。它设有一个由十一名成员组成的总办事处，其中一人担任主任。委员会主任月薪600元，外加每月2,000元的联络津贴，而委员每人月薪300元，总办事处成员每人月薪100元。据说，原上海市政府的一名教育官员，目前失业，已被收买并担任委员会主任一职。

另据悉，委员会雇员在就职前，均被要求宣誓并承诺支持汪精卫。
委员会成员已请求各学校支持和平运动，并向每所在委员会发出的印刷表格上盖章的学校提供50元，但所有这些活动均以失败告终。此外，由于委员会成员内部不和以及利润分配不均，发生了严重分裂，该委员会可能不久将被解散。
